subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a synchronous public plugin/API veto point for persistent config writes, and what trust, redaction, timeout, and failure semantics should it use?
rationale: Automation can prove the source gap, but it cannot safely choose a plugin API contract that can observe or block sensitive auth/provider config and affect Gateway availability.

options.title: Design the config-write veto API
options.body: Define a typed pre-persistence hook with explicit ordering, timeouts, redaction/SecretRef rules, actor metadata, fail-closed behavior, and coverage across config.set, config.patch, config.apply, and shared mutation helpers.

options.title: Keep validation built in only
options.body: Reject the public hook direction and continue improving core validation, doctor, and gateway-tool guards while leaving external validators as advisory tools agents must call explicitly.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Defer this hook until the broader validation/preflight framework chooses one boundary for boot-time checks, config writes, and plugin-owned validators.

recommendation.title: Design the config-write veto API
recommendation.body: Define a typed pre-persistence hook with explicit ordering, timeouts, redaction/SecretRef rules, actor metadata, fail-closed behavior, and coverage across config.set, config.patch, config.apply, and shared mutation helpers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the prior keep-open product-routing review and has recent adjacent config-write safety history.
